title: Post-Discharge Follow-Up Calls
summary: Scripted follow-up calls after discharge, in the patient's language, that check medicines, follow-up visits and clinician-defined warning signs and hand any concern to a nurse.

seo.title: Post-Discharge Follow-Up Voice Calls | VipraTech
seo.description: Outbound voice agent that calls discharged patients with clinician-approved scripts, checks medicines and follow-ups, and escalates concerns to nurses.

designed_for: Care Coordination or Patient Experience Manager

problem.intro: The days after discharge are when patients are unsure about medicines, miss follow-up visits or notice symptoms they do not know how to judge. Many hospitals intend to call every discharged patient, but nurses and coordinators cannot reach everyone, and the calls that do happen are rarely recorded in a structured way.

pain_points.title: Coverage gaps
pain_points.detail: Follow-up calls happen when staff have time, so many discharged patients are never called.

pain_points.title: Late detection of concerns
pain_points.detail: A patient who has not started their medicines or has a warning sign may only come to notice at readmission.

pain_points.title: Unstructured notes
pain_points.detail: Call outcomes sit in registers or free-text notes, so quality teams cannot see patterns by department.

pain_points.title: Language and hearing barriers
pain_points.detail: Elderly patients and family members need slow, clear calls in their own language, at times that suit them.

solution.overview: We build an outbound voice agent that calls discharged patients, or their nominated caregiver, at intervals your clinical team sets. It follows a script approved by your doctors and nursing leadership for that department: whether medicines were collected and are being taken as prescribed, whether the follow-up appointment is booked, and a set of yes-or-no questions about warning signs your clinicians define. Answers are recorded in structured form. Any yes to a warning-sign question, any confusion about medicines or any request to speak to someone creates an immediate task for a nurse, who calls back. The agent never interprets symptoms or gives advice.
capabilities: Outbound calls at clinician-set intervals after discharge, with retry rules and caregiver contacts
Department-specific scripts approved by doctors and nursing leadership
Structured capture of medicine collection, adherence questions and follow-up booking status
Clinician-defined warning-sign questions with immediate escalation on any positive answer
Follow-up appointment booking or rebooking during the call
Department dashboards for quality and patient experience teams

workflow.title: Schedule from discharge data
workflow.detail: Discharged patients, their department, follow-up date and preferred language are pulled from the HIS.

workflow.title: Call the patient or caregiver
workflow.detail: The agent calls at the agreed interval and confirms it is speaking with the patient or the nominated caregiver.

workflow.title: Run the approved script
workflow.detail: It asks about medicines, the follow-up visit and the department's warning-sign questions.

workflow.title: Escalate concerns
workflow.detail: Any warning sign, confusion or request for a person creates an urgent nurse task with the call summary.

workflow.title: Book the follow-up
workflow.detail: If the follow-up visit is not booked, the agent offers slots and books one.

workflow.title: Record and close
workflow.detail: Structured answers go to the care coordination dashboard, and nurses close every escalation.

inputs: Discharge list with department, diagnosis category and follow-up date
Patient and caregiver contact details and preferred language
Department scripts and warning-sign questions approved by clinicians
outputs: Structured call outcome for each patient
Urgent nurse tasks with call summaries
human_in_the_loop: Clinicians write and approve every script and warning-sign question, and a nurse calls back on every escalation. The agent does not interpret answers clinically or tell a patient what to do about a symptom; it routes concerns to people.
integrations: WhatsApp Business API for follow-up confirmations
Nursing task or care coordination tool
guardrails: Script-bound dialogue, so the agent cannot improvise medical content
Any positive warning-sign answer escalates, with no model judgement on severity
Emergency phrases trigger direction to emergency care and an immediate staff alert
Identity check before any health information is discussed
Calls only within agreed hours and stopped at the patient's request
compliance_notes: Patient consent for follow-up calls captured and recorded at discharge, in line with the DPDP Act 2023.
Designed as a communication aid; clinical assessment of every escalation stays with nurses and doctors.
Structured outcomes can support the follow-up and patient feedback evidence used in accreditation reviews such as NABH.

pilot.scope: Follow-up calls for patients discharged from one or two departments, using a script approved by the department head, with nurses handling every escalation.
deliverables: Approved department scripts and warning-sign lists
Outbound agent connected to discharge data
Pilot review with clinical and quality leads

what_we_measure.how: Discharged patients successfully contacted, compared with the manual call register before the pilot.
Time from escalation to nurse callback, and nurse judgement of whether each escalation was appropriate.
Patients without a booked follow-up who were booked during the call.
Clinical review of a sample of calls against the approved script.

faqs.q: Does the AI decide whether a symptom is serious?
faqs.a: No. Clinicians define the questions, and any positive answer goes to a nurse. The agent does not grade severity or advise the patient.

faqs.q: Who receives the call if the patient is elderly or unwell?
faqs.a: You can record a nominated caregiver at discharge. The agent confirms who it is speaking with and follows your rules on what can be discussed with a caregiver.
Hindi, English and Hinglish, plus the regional languages of your catchment area. Scripts in each language are translated and approved by clinicians before use.

faqs.q: What happens if the patient asks a medical question?
faqs.a: The agent explains that a nurse will call back, records the question in a task and continues the script. It never answers clinical questions itself.
